questions.question: What is the relationship between Doppler frequency shift f_d and radial velocity v_r at radar wavelength λ?
options: v_r = f_d * λ
questions.explanation: The standard Doppler radial velocity equation is v_r = (f_d * λ) / 2.

questions.question: Which radar moment is primarily used to identify hail cores in severe convective storms?
options: Differential Reflectivity (Z_DR) and High MAX(Z)
Low PRF single pulse
Ground clutter filter only
Radial velocity zero-crossing
questions.explanation: Hail cores exhibit high horizontal reflectivity MAX(Z) > 55 dBZ paired with low Z_DR near 0 dB due to tumbling motion.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Background Error Covariance matrix (B-Matrix) in 4D-Var?
options: Spreads observation increments spatially and across physical variables
Multiplies satellite brightness directly
Computes friction velocity
Eliminates grid points
questions.explanation: The B-matrix governs how observation innovations are projected in physical and spatial space.

questions.question: Why is the adjoint operator required during 4D-Var optimization?
options: To compute the gradient of the cost function with respect to initial state efficiently
To invert radar frequency
To increase time step indefinitely
To avoid matrix multiplication
questions.explanation: The adjoint model integrates backward in time to yield the exact cost function gradient in a single backward sweep.

questionBank.question: In operational NWP primitive equations, which vertical coordinate transformation is terrain-following?
options: Sigma Coordinate: σ = (p - p_top) / (p_sfc - p_top)
Geometric Height z strictly above mean sea level
Dry Static Energy Coordinate in the troposphere
Geopotential Thickness Coordinate with fixed top
questionBank.explanation: Sigma terrain-following coordinates normalize surface pressure variations, mapping complex mountain topography cleanly onto a horizontal computational plane σ = 1.

questionBank.question: Why does the Arakawa C-grid staggering yield optimal gravity wave dispersion in hydrostatic atmospheric models?
options: It isolates mass and wind variables on opposite corners
Velocity components u and v are staggered at the respective flux cell faces while mass/pressure h resides at the center
It avoids solving the horizontal pressure gradient term altogether
It forces velocity to zero along closed physical domain boundaries
questionBank.explanation: The Arakawa C-grid evaluates divergence and pressure gradients over minimum grid distance Δx, preventing false 2Δx computational checkerboard modes.

questionBank.question: What numerical stability condition dictates maximum permissible time step Δt in explicit advection schemes?
options: Boussinesq Incompressibility Criterion
Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy (CFL) Condition: C = u * Δt / Δx ≤ 1
Navier-Stokes Reynolds Limit: Re ≤ 2000
Planck Radiative Equilibrium Balance: F = σT^4
questionBank.explanation: The CFL condition requires that the numerical domain of dependence completely contains the physical domain of dependence (C ≤ 1 for explicit stability).

questionBank.question: In 4D-Var Data Assimilation, what is the core role of the Adjoint Model?
options: To extrapolate infrared satellite brightness temperatures over desert surfaces
To integrate sensitivities of the cost function backwards in time to obtain gradient vectors with respect to initial state
To filter high-frequency tidal oscillations in the stratosphere
To perform horizontal bi-linear interpolation on irregular grids
questionBank.explanation: The adjoint model integrates backward through the assimilation window, computing exact gradients of the observation misfit cost function for minimization.

questionBank.question: Why are raw satellite radiances (Level 1B/1C) assimilated directly into NWP via RTTOV/CRTM instead of retrieved Level 2 products?
options: Retrieved Level 2 products contain correlated observational errors and unrepresented prior assumptions
Raw radiances require zero compute power to ingest
Level 2 products only work during daytime solar illumination
Satellite sensors cannot measure radiance over land
questionBank.explanation: Direct assimilation of radiances using Fast Radiative Transfer models (RTTOV/CRTM) avoids non-linear retrieval error correlation and ensures consistency with model physics.

questionBank.question: What physical hydrometeor property is directly quantified by Differential Reflectivity (ZDR = 10 * log10(Zh / Zv))?
options: Total water vapor column density
Median shape eccentricity/oblateness of falling hydrometeors
Radial Doppler velocity toward the radar transmitter
Surface rainfall accumulation rate strictly in mm/hr
questionBank.explanation: Large raindrops flatten into oblate spheroids due to aerodynamic drag as they fall, causing Zh > Zv and producing positive ZDR values (e.g. +1 to +4 dB).

questionBank.question: In pulsed Doppler radars, how are maximum unambiguous range (Rmax) and maximum unambiguous velocity (Vmax) related?
options: Rmax * Vmax = c * λ / 8 (Doppler Dilemma)
Rmax + Vmax = constant frequency
Rmax * Vmax = PRF^2
Velocity is completely independent of maximum range
questionBank.explanation: The Doppler Dilemma states that increasing pulse repetition frequency (PRF) extends Vmax but simultaneously reduces unambiguous range Rmax.

questionBank.question: Which radar signature on reflectivity and Doppler velocity indicates a high-risk supercell mesocyclone?
options: Stratiform bright band melting layer at 4 km AGL
Hook Echo on Reflectivity paired with a cyclonic Inbound/Outbound Velocity Couplet
Uniform horizontal velocity azimuth display (VAD)
Zero differential phase shift KDP across all elevation scans
questionBank.explanation: A hook echo wrapping around the storm rear flank downdraft alongside adjacent inbound and outbound radial velocity maxima confirms strong rotating mesocyclonic updraft.

questionBank.question: Which dual-pol signature uniquely separates large tumbling hailstones from torrential rain?
options: Very high reflectivity (>55 dBZ) paired with near-zero Differential Reflectivity (ZDR ≈ 0 dB)
Negative reflectivity with high correlation coefficient
Extremely positive ZDR (>5.0 dB) with zero reflectivity
Infinite specific differential phase KDP
questionBank.explanation: Tumbling hailstones present no preferred orientation to the radar beam, resulting in isotropic scattering (ZDR ≈ 0 dB) despite extremely high total reflectivity (>55 dBZ).

questionBank.question: In the Dvorak Enhanced Infrared (EIR) technique, what does a persistent cold Central Dense Overcast (CDO) surrounding a distinct warm eye indicate?
options: Rapid extratropical transition with severe dry air entrainment
Strong convective core organization corresponding to a high T-Number (Severe Cyclonic Storm)
Weakening depression with low level circulation center exposed
Subtropical anticyclone subsidence
questionBank.explanation: A symmetrical cold CDO surrounding a warm eye indicates vigorous eyewall convection, low central pressure, and severe cyclonic intensity (T4.0 - T6.5).

questionBank.question: Which quadrant of a northward-moving tropical cyclone in the Northern Hemisphere experiences the maximum storm surge and onshore wind forcing?
options: Rear left quadrant (Southwest)
Right-front quadrant (Northeast)
Rear right quadrant (Southeast)
Left-front quadrant (Northwest)
questionBank.explanation: In the Northern Hemisphere, cyclonic rotation is counter-clockwise. The forward translation speed adds directly to rotational winds in the right-front quadrant, maximizing wind stress and storm surge.

questionBank.subjectName: Subject 2: Storm Surge Modeling & Coastal Impact
questionBank.question: How does shallow coastal bathymetry (such as the northern Bay of Bengal shelf) amplify peak storm surge heights?
options: It prevents sea surface water from returning via deep gravitational undertow, piling water against the coast
It suppresses surface wind stress completely
It eliminates astronomical tide interaction
It converts cyclonic vortex momentum into seismic waves
questionBank.explanation: Shallow continental shelves restrict deep barotropic return flow, forcing wind-driven surface waters to pile up rapidly against the coastline.

questionBank.subjectName: Subject 1: INSAT-3DR Imager Channels & Cloud Classification
questionBank.question: Which channel on the INSAT-3DR imager is most effective for distinguishing daytime low-level water fog from snow and ice clouds?
options: Shortwave Infrared (SWIR 1.6 µm)
Thermal Infrared 1 (TIR-1 10.8 µm)
Visible (VIS 0.65 µm)
Water Vapor (WV 6.7 µm)
questionBank.explanation: Ice crystals absorb strongly at 1.6 µm (appearing very dark in SWIR), while liquid water droplets reflect solar SWIR strongly (appearing bright).

questionBank.question: How does the INSAT-3DR 19-channel sounder derive vertical Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE)?
options: By integrating the temperature and moisture soundings from surface to equilibrium level
By measuring surface radar backscatter
By direct optical counting of lightning flashes
By calculating ocean surface salinity gradients
questionBank.explanation: The atmospheric sounder retrieves vertical profiles of temperature T(p) and dewpoint Td(p), allowing numerical integration of buoyant parcel ascent energy (CAPE).

questionBank.question: During a 'Break Monsoon' phase over India, where does the main axis of the Monsoon Trough shift?
options: Northward towards the foothills of the Himalayas
Southward into the central Arabian Sea
Eastward over the Andaman Sea
Westward over the Thar Desert
questionBank.explanation: During break spells, the monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, causing rainfall suppression over central India and intense orographic precipitation along Himalayan catchments.

questionBank.question: What sea surface temperature pattern defines a Positive Indian Ocean Dipole (+IOD)?
options: Anomalously warm SST in the western Indian Ocean and cool SST in the eastern equatorial Indian Ocean
Uniform warming across the entire Bay of Bengal
Cool SST near Madagascar and warm SST off Sumatra
Strong negative thermocline tilt in the eastern Pacific
questionBank.explanation: A positive IOD features warmer waters near the African coast (western pole) and cooler waters near Sumatra/Indonesia, which favors enhanced Indian summer monsoon rainfall.

Navier-Stokes Reynolds Limit: Re ≤ 2000
Planck Radiative Equilibrium Balance: F = σT^4
questions.explanation: The CFL condition requires that the numerical domain of dependence completely contains the physical domain of dependence (C ≤ 1 for explicit stability).

questions.question: In 4D-Var Data Assimilation, what is the core role of the Adjoint Model?
options: To extrapolate infrared satellite brightness temperatures over desert surfaces
To integrate sensitivities of the cost function backwards in time to obtain gradient vectors with respect to initial state
To filter high-frequency tidal oscillations in the stratosphere
To perform horizontal bi-linear interpolation on irregular grids
questions.explanation: The adjoint model integrates backward through the assimilation window, computing exact gradients of the observation misfit cost function for minimization.

questions.subjectName: Subject 1: INSAT-3DR Imager Channels & Cloud Classification
questions.question: Which channel on the INSAT-3DR imager is most effective for distinguishing daytime low-level water fog from snow and ice clouds?
options: Shortwave Infrared (SWIR 1.6 µm)
Thermal Infrared 1 (TIR-1 10.8 µm)
Visible (VIS 0.65 µm)
Water Vapor (WV 6.7 µm)
questions.explanation: Ice crystals absorb strongly at 1.6 µm (appearing very dark in SWIR), while liquid water droplets reflect solar SWIR strongly (appearing bright).

questions.question: How does the INSAT-3DR 19-channel sounder derive vertical Convective Available Potential Energy (CAPE)?
options: By integrating the temperature and moisture soundings from surface to equilibrium level
By measuring surface radar backscatter
By direct optical counting of lightning flashes
By calculating ocean surface salinity gradients
questions.explanation: The atmospheric sounder retrieves vertical profiles of temperature T(p) and dewpoint Td(p), allowing numerical integration of buoyant parcel ascent energy (CAPE).

questions.question: In operational NWP primitive equations, which vertical coordinate transformation is terrain-following?
options: Sigma Coordinate: σ = (p - p_top) / (p_sfc - p_top)
Geometric Height z strictly above mean sea level
Dry Static Energy Coordinate in the troposphere
Geopotential Thickness Coordinate with fixed top
questions.explanation: Sigma terrain-following coordinates normalize surface pressure variations, mapping complex mountain topography cleanly onto a horizontal computational plane σ = 1.

questions.question: Why are raw satellite radiances (Level 1B/1C) assimilated directly into NWP via RTTOV/CRTM instead of retrieved Level 2 products?
options: Retrieved Level 2 products contain correlated observational errors and unrepresented prior assumptions
Raw radiances require zero compute power to ingest
Level 2 products only work during daytime solar illumination
Satellite sensors cannot measure radiance over land
questions.explanation: Direct assimilation of radiances using Fast Radiative Transfer models (RTTOV/CRTM) avoids non-linear retrieval error correlation and ensures consistency with model physics.

questions.question: What physical hydrometeor property is directly quantified by Differential Reflectivity (ZDR = 10 * log10(Zh / Zv))?
options: Total water vapor column density
Median shape eccentricity/oblateness of falling hydrometeors
Radial Doppler velocity toward the radar transmitter
Surface rainfall accumulation rate strictly in mm/hr
questions.explanation: Large raindrops flatten into oblate spheroids due to aerodynamic drag as they fall, causing Zh > Zv and producing positive ZDR values (e.g. +1 to +4 dB).

questions.question: In the Dvorak Enhanced Infrared (EIR) technique, what does a persistent cold Central Dense Overcast (CDO) surrounding a distinct warm eye indicate?
options: Rapid extratropical transition with severe dry air entrainment
Strong convective core organization corresponding to a high T-Number (Severe Cyclonic Storm)
Weakening depression with low level circulation center exposed
Subtropical anticyclone subsidence
questions.explanation: A symmetrical cold CDO surrounding a warm eye indicates vigorous eyewall convection, low central pressure, and severe cyclonic intensity (T4.0 - T6.5).

questions.question: During a 'Break Monsoon' phase over India, where does the main axis of the Monsoon Trough shift?
options: Northward towards the foothills of the Himalayas
Southward into the central Arabian Sea
Eastward over the Andaman Sea
Westward over the Thar Desert
questions.explanation: During break spells, the monsoon trough shifts to the Himalayan foothills, causing rainfall suppression over central India and intense orographic precipitation along Himalayan catchments.

questions.question: What sea surface temperature pattern defines a Positive Indian Ocean Dipole (+IOD)?
options: Anomalously warm SST in the western Indian Ocean and cool SST in the eastern equatorial Indian Ocean
Uniform warming across the entire Bay of Bengal
Cool SST near Madagascar and warm SST off Sumatra
Strong negative thermocline tilt in the eastern Pacific
questions.explanation: A positive IOD features warmer waters near the African coast (western pole) and cooler waters near Sumatra/Indonesia, which favors enhanced Indian summer monsoon rainfall.

questions.question: Why does the Arakawa C-grid staggering yield optimal gravity wave dispersion in hydrostatic atmospheric models?
options: It isolates mass and wind variables on opposite corners
Velocity components u and v are staggered at the respective flux cell faces while mass/pressure h resides at the center
It avoids solving the horizontal pressure gradient term altogether
It forces velocity to zero along closed physical domain boundaries
questions.explanation: The Arakawa C-grid evaluates divergence and pressure gradients over minimum grid distance Δx, preventing false 2Δx computational checkerboard modes.

questions.question: Which radar signature on reflectivity and Doppler velocity indicates a high-risk supercell mesocyclone?
options: Stratiform bright band melting layer at 4 km AGL
Hook Echo on Reflectivity paired with a cyclonic Inbound/Outbound Velocity Couplet
Uniform horizontal velocity azimuth display (VAD)
Zero differential phase shift KDP across all elevation scans
questions.explanation: A hook echo wrapping around the storm rear flank downdraft alongside adjacent inbound and outbound radial velocity maxima confirms strong rotating mesocyclonic updraft.
